decisions.decision: How does a user explicitly ask stackgen to install an optional tool?
decisions.ruling: A tools menu with one multi-select list of optional tools and no item preselected. Only the tools the user picks are installed. The pick is recorded in addons:; a re-run shows the current pick and asks only whether to change it.
decisions.rejected: Keep each tool on its pack with a consent line that defaults to no; or never offer the tools and install one only when the user names it

decisions.decision: Where do the picked MCP servers land?
decisions.ruling: Every picked MCP server (context7, notion) lands in the vwf-tools local plugin, user scope, like the LSP servers. The pick is the product's, committed in .config/vwf.yaml's addons:; each person's machine gets the servers in their own vwf-tools when they run /vwf:setup.
decisions.rejected: Per-tool scope: context7 in vwf-tools, notion in the repo's .mcp.json

decisions.decision: What happens to the claude-design pack's MCP server?
decisions.ruling: It moves to vwf-tools and stays required: the claude-design pack declares it under user_mcp_servers:, so it lands in vwf-tools whenever the pack is picked, with no tools-menu step.
decisions.rejected: Leave it in .mcp.json and let B106 decide

decisions.decision: What happens to the project-scoped mcp_servers: key?
decisions.ruling: Retire it: remove the mcp_servers: key, the .mcp.json write path and its tier-2 consent line from the pack format, the materializer and the generator. user_mcp_servers: is the only MCP key. stackgen-sync removes a repo's recorded .mcp.json entries, behind consent.
decisions.rejected: Keep the key and the .mcp.json path, unused

decisions.decision: What is the name of the one MCP key left?
decisions.ruling: user_mcp_servers: keeps its name.
decisions.rejected: Rename it mcp_servers:, which gives an old lockfile's mcp_servers list two meanings

decisions.decision: Where are the optional tools defined?
decisions.ruling: Each optional tool is a pack and a bundle of a new type, kind and axis named addon, with no default: true: plugins/stackgen/stacks/addon/context7 (user_mcp_servers:), addon/notion (moved from capability-provider/notion, its skill and its server), addon/taste-skill (a ## Claude plugins section). The tools menu lists the bundles of the addon axis. assets/kinds.md gains an addon kind. The name addon keeps the axis apart from the existing phrase 'the three tool axes' (design, cicd, stylesheet), which stays as it is. addon counts as an axis: every 'seven axes' count becomes eight.
decisions.rejected: One tools catalog file beside the packs; notion kept at capability-provider/notion; naming the axis tool and rewording the three tool axes as token axes

decisions.decision: Where is the user's pick recorded?
decisions.ruling: A top-level addons: list in .config/vwf.yaml, one per product, for example addons: [context7, notion]. Absent or empty means no optional tool. The name addons: keeps it apart from the existing repo.stack.tools key; the menu is still shown to the user as optional tools.
decisions.rejected: Per project, projects.<name>.stack.tools; a top-level tools: key, easy to confuse with repo.stack.tools

decisions.decision: Which command shows the tools menu and writes addons:?
decisions.ruling: /vwf:architecture shows the tools menu after the stack menu and writes addons:. /vwf:setup materializes each picked tool on every run and removes a dropped one.
decisions.rejected: /vwf:setup alone shows the menu and installs

decisions.decision: What does the stackgen generator do when the user did not pick context7?
decisions.ruling: The generator halts only when no Context7 server is reachable from any source (the context7 addon in vwf-tools, a user-level MCP, another plugin), keeping the rule never to write from training knowledge, and says: add context7 through /vwf:architecture's tools menu, run /vwf:setup, restart the session. The menu text says that generation needs context7. A duplicate registration is the user's choice; the plan says nothing about it.
decisions.rejected: Fall back to WebFetch research; or offer context7 at the point of need

decisions.decision: What does design-session do when taste-skill is not picked?
decisions.ruling: It halts as today, with the new remedy: add taste-skill through /vwf:architecture's tools menu, run /vwf:setup, restart. The tools menu says that the claude-code design tool needs it. The three import skills do not need taste-skill and keep working.
decisions.rejected: design-session works without taste-skill

decisions.decision: How does the taste-skill tool pack install the plugin?
decisions.ruling: Through the bootstrap handoff, as today: the addon/taste-skill pack carries the ## Claude plugins section, and the materializer hands it to bootstrap through docs/sync/vwf.md. vwf-tools holds servers only.
decisions.rejected: vwf-tools declares a dependency on taste-skill@taste-skill, a reversal of the 2026-10-24 packs-hand-off-to-bootstrap decision

decisions.decision: What does /vwf:setup's migrate path do for an existing shaped repo?
decisions.ruling: Keep what the repo has: migrate writes into addons: each tool the repo already records (notion from backing_template or the lockfile's mcp_servers, taste-skill from the lockfile's bootstrap block; claude-design moves to vwf-tools with its pack). For context7, which every vwf user had, it asks one yes/no question. It renames the lockfile's local_plugin block from stackgen-lsp to vwf-tools and moves the recorded .mcp.json entries to vwf-tools, behind consent.
decisions.rejected: Start clean with addons: [] and print what was removed

decisions.decision: What does /vwf:doctor report about addons:?
decisions.ruling: Drift, never blocking: a picked tool that is not installed, or an installed tool that is not picked, is a drift finding, remedied by /vwf:setup. A missing tool never blocks execute; the generator and design-session halt on their own.
decisions.rejected: No check

decisions.decision: Does the vwf.yaml change bump config_format?
decisions.ruling: Yes, to 25: the migration moves notion out of projects.<name>.stack.backing_template into addons:, which is not additive. The format-lineage row for 25 names the move, the addons: key and the context7 question.
decisions.rejected: An additive key with no bump, which leaves a notion pin on the backing axis with no reader

decisions.decision: What command does the context7 pack declare?
decisions.ruling: The command vwf's manifest declares today, unchanged, moved under user_mcp_servers: context7 in the context7 addon pack. The literal entry is the fenced YAML block in U3's edit 4.
decisions.rejected: A new runner or a pinned version

decisions.decision: Are the about 130 pack hints that say API reference belongs to Context7 at use time swept?
decisions.ruling: No. They are hints with no call and no halt; they stay. A sweep is parked.
decisions.rejected: Sweep every pack file in this plan

decisions.decision: Who regenerates inventory.md?
decisions.ruling: U3, as its last step, with mise x -- mise run p:plugins:inventory: the pre-commit inventory hook needs each new or moved pack, its bundle, its pack.yaml version, kinds.md and inventory.md in one commit. U3 also bumps the versions of the packs it changes. This is the one generator a non-gates unit runs.
decisions.rejected: Split the packs across units and regenerate in the gates unit, which fails the hook on the first pack commit

decisions.decision: Does the plan carry a review unit?
decisions.ruling: One review unit, U8, in wave 2, covering U1 to U5: U3 edits scripts/src/check.ts and its test, which is runnable code. It covers edit units alone, so it runs the security half.
decisions.rejected: No review unit

decisions.decision: What does stackgen do with an already registered stackgen-lsp plugin?
decisions.ruling: On the first materialization or sync that finds ~/.claude/plugins/local/stackgen-lsp/, stackgen offers one tier-3 migration, in this order: write ~/.claude/plugins/local/vwf-tools/ with the union of both manifests' servers; register vwf-tools; claude plugin uninstall stackgen-lsp@stackgen-lsp --scope user; claude plugin marketplace remove stackgen-lsp; delete the old directory. Each step checks its own result first and is skipped when already done. When a step fails or its printed command is declined, stackgen stops and reports; doctor shows drift; the next run continues from the first incomplete step. Both plugins may serve a server in that window. A decline of the whole offer is D27.
decisions.rejected: Leave the old plugin registered beside vwf-tools, which serves each LSP twice

decisions.decision: How are the claude-design server tool names written, and does the checker design-tool MCP guard see them?
decisions.ruling: Inside vwf-tools, Claude names the server tools mcp__plugin_vwf-tools_claude-design__<op>; canvas-push.md and every claude-design skill state that form. U3 widens the guard in scripts/src/check.ts (:2326-2343) to match mcp__plugin_vwf-tools_<token>__ beside the forms it matches today, drops the .mcp.json wording of its comment at :2335, and adds a case for the new form to scripts/src/check.test.ts.
decisions.rejected: Leave scripts/src out of scope, with the guard blind to the new name

decisions.decision: Which source adds notion to addons: at migration?
decisions.ruling: Either source: notion is added to addons: when any projects.<name>.stack.backing_template list names the slug notion, or any repo's stackgen lockfile in the product records the capability-provider/notion pack or its .mcp.json server.
decisions.rejected: backing_template only, with a lockfile-only entry removed as a leftover

decisions.decision: What does a second repo do when this machine is already migrated?
decisions.ruling: When the lockfile still names stackgen-lsp and ~/.claude/plugins/local/stackgen-lsp/ does not exist — another repo already migrated this machine, or the machine never had it — the lockfile's local_plugin block is rewritten to the vwf-tools names without a prompt. The repo's servers then merge into vwf-tools behind the normal tier-3 consent, as a first write when vwf-tools does not exist yet.
decisions.rejected: A consent line for the lockfile rewrite in every repo

decisions.decision: How does a re-sync handle an item that moves from an old pin to a new pin?
decisions.ruling: No general net diff. stackgen-sync carries a fixed relocation table: capability-provider/notion -> addon/notion, and the taste-skill@taste-skill claim of design-tool/claude-code@1 -> addon/taste-skill. In the base repo, a relocated item is re-attributed in the lockfile, never removed and re-added; a change of place (.mcp.json to vwf-tools) or of content (the notion skill's paths: key) is a normal update behind its normal consent. In a member repo, D29 applies instead: the old items are removed. The lockfile records the owners of every item as a list: local_plugin servers as {name, packs: [...]}; bootstrap.plugins keeps its existing map, whose components: [...] list is the owners list; skill entries by their component. An old-shape entry with no owners is read with owners unknown and rewritten on the next sync. Doctor reads the owners from the lockfile and skips an entry whose owners are unknown.
decisions.rejected: A general net diff over old and new pins, which no single setup call can compute; remove then re-add; one owner per item

decisions.decision: Does the tools round offer defer?
decisions.ruling: No. addons: is always a list, [] when none; it never holds unresolved, and doctor never reports [] as a pending decision.
decisions.rejected: Offer defer and write addons: unresolved

decisions.decision: In a multi-repo product, which repo does /vwf:setup materialize addon pins into?
decisions.ruling: The base repo only. Its stackgen lockfile records the addon claims, and doctor reads the base repo's lockfile for the addons check. Members get no addon skill files; the servers are user scope anyway.
decisions.rejected: Every repo of the product materializes every addon

decisions.decision: What happens to a shared vwf-tools server when one repo drops it and another still claims it?
decisions.ruling: vwf-tools keeps a claims file inside its manifest folder, ~/.claude/plugins/local/vwf-tools/.claude-plugin/claims.json, mapping each server key (MCP and LSP) to the list of absolute repo paths that claim it, so the rule that stackgen writes outside the repo only under .claude-plugin/ stays. A materialization adds this repo's path; a removal drops only this repo's path and deletes the key from the manifest only when no repo claims it. An absent claims.json means every key is unclaimed and kept. Any write drops a claimed repo path that no longer exists on disk.
decisions.rejected: Removal deletes the key; the other repo's next /vwf:setup re-adds it

decisions.decision: What happens when the user declines the stackgen-lsp to vwf-tools migration?
decisions.ruling: Nothing is written: vwf-tools is not written or registered, and stackgen-lsp stays as it is, so no server is served twice. Newly picked addon servers and the claude-design server land nowhere until the migration is accepted, and the repo's .mcp.json entries are kept: their removal is not offered until the migration is accepted. The migration is offered again on each later setup or sync until it is accepted; doctor reports the old directory and the unlanded servers as drift. A sync runs the migration offer whenever the stackgen-lsp directory exists, even in a repo whose lockfile has no local_plugin block. When the user accepts the migration but declines the separate .mcp.json key-removal line, the lockfile keeps its top-level mcp_servers list and the removal is offered again on the next run.
decisions.rejected: Record the decline and never offer again

decisions.decision: Does the checker's stdio runner guard cover the context7 runner once it moves into a pack?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U3 points the guard in scripts/src/check.ts (:2226-2281) also at every pack's user_mcp_servers: stdio entries — every runner behind a ${VAR:-default} expansion — keeps the manifest path, and adds one test case in scripts/src/check.test.ts.
decisions.rejected: Leave the guard on manifests only and park it

decisions.decision: Which lockfiles does the migration read in a multi-repo product, and what happens to a member repo's old items?
decisions.ruling: The migration reads the stackgen lockfiles of every repo of the product that is cloned locally (base and members) for notion and taste-skill (D12, D21); a member not cloned locally is skipped with a one-line warning. A member repo's old items (the notion skill files, its .mcp.json entry) are removed by that member's own sync, behind consent; the relocation table applies in the base repo only. A bootstrap plugin that another repo of the product claims through an addon pack (taste-skill through the base repo's addon/taste-skill) is never removed by a member's handoff removal.
decisions.rejected: Read the base lockfile only; leave member items in place

decisions.decision: How is claims.json seeded at the stackgen-lsp migration?
decisions.ruling: The migration seeds claims.json with the current repo's path for each key the current repo's lockfile claims; other repos add their claims on their next sync. An inherited key no repo claims is never deleted automatically; doctor reports it as drift.
decisions.rejected: Seed no claims and delete unclaimed keys on the first removal

decisions.decision: What does the menu contract in stack-adapter.md say about the addon round?
decisions.ruling: U4 adds to the menu-payload contract (stack-adapter.md:175-188) the addon round's shape: product-level, multi-select, no default, no generate entry, no defer, and an optional needed_by string on each entry naming the shipped pack that needs it.
decisions.rejected: Only the addon enum value in the contract
